summary: @servicetitan/intl preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: The package's `preinstall` script runs `node setup.mjs`, which downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases at install time and invokes `execFileSync(bun, ['math_init.js'])` against a ~727KB obfuscated sibling file `math_init.js`. Both `setup.mjs` and `math_init.js` are heavily obfuscated: `setup.mjs` uses `_0x`-style identifier renaming and a per-function string-table dispatch; `math_init.js` starts with `// @bun @bun-cjs` and uses a shuffled string-array plus decoder function (`hc1jfK9`, `WV8StW`) matching the obfuscator.io shape. An i18n library has no legitimate need to install a second language runtime at install time to execute an opaque payload. This gives the publisher arbitrary code execution on every installer's machine at `npm install` time, invoked through an alternate runtime that bypasses Node-based tooling and static review of the payload.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
